newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins fluctuate on Yeltsin op worries.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins fluctuate on Yeltsin op worries.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds rose in early trading on local buying, then eased as the market felt uneasy after media reports of new doubts about President Boris Yeltsin's health but bounced back later on an official denial, dealers said.

Russian financial markets became nervous after a Moscow radio station report that Yeltsin was too sick to undergo planned heart surgery because his haemoglobin levels were too low. The head of Yeltsin's press office flatly denied the reports.

"Russian banks were supporting the market in early trading, especially the fourth tranche at 59.25. But there was no active buying after Western operators stepped in," Sberbank dealer Pavel Sool said.
Another dealer said: "What we have seen today is active buying from some banks in early trading and profit-taking from others later."
Dealers said MinFin prices had eased up to 0.9 point on the rumours about Yeltsin's health but then edged up on the official denial.
"Prices have bounced back but they are lower than opening levels," one dealer said.
Sool said price levels were going down gently as there was no active investor demand.
"But there is no active selling either," he added.
